nodes.label: 2-Channel 5V Relay Module
nodes.description: Annotated callout diagram (labelled product photo) of a blue/black 2-channel relay board. Two blue Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C relays rated 10A 250VAC / 10A 125VAC / 10A 30VDC / 10A 28VDC sit over two screw terminal blocks. Labelled parts: NO/COM/NC contacts per channel, control header GND/IN1/IN2/VCC, a second GND/VCC/JD-VCC header, a power-select jumper, and per-channel relay switch indicator LEDs.
nodes.rationale: A relay module is used so that low-voltage 3.3V/5V logic from the controller can switch mains-voltage actuators safely; the two channels give independent control of two distinct actuators from one board.

nodes.label: Optocoupler Isolation and JD-VCC Power-Select Jumper
nodes.description: The board carries per-channel optoisolators between the IN pins and the relay coil drivers, plus a 'power select jumper' bridging VCC and JD-VCC. Removing the jumper separates the logic supply (VCC) from the relay coil supply (JD-VCC).
nodes.rationale: Galvanically separating coil current from the controller's 5V rail prevents relay switching transients and inrush from browning out or resetting the single-board computer, which is the classic failure mode when driving inductive mains loads from a Pi.

nodes.label: NO / COM / NC Contact Scheme
nodes.description: Each channel exposes a normally-open, common and normally-closed screw terminal, so a load can be wired to be either energised-on-command or energised-by-default and interrupted on command.
nodes.rationale: Wiring choice encodes the fail-safe behaviour: a load on NO defaults to OFF if the controller dies, a load on NC defaults to ON — critical when deciding whether ventilation or heating should persist during a controller failure.

nodes.label: IN1 / IN2 Active-Low Control Inputs
nodes.description: Two logic-level control lines on the GND/IN1/IN2/VCC header. Each drives one relay channel and its indicator LED. Modules of this family are conventionally active-low (pull IN low to energise the coil).
nodes.rationale: Active-low convention is noted because inverted control polarity is a common integration bug: a GPIO that boots low would energise the relay before software starts.

nodes.label: Low-Voltage-to-Mains Load Switching Pattern
nodes.description: Architectural pattern in which a 3.3V/5V GPIO signal from the controller drives an optoisolated relay coil, whose 10A/250VAC dry contacts carry the mains circuit of a household appliance.
nodes.rationale: Keeps all mains wiring off the computing board entirely; the only coupling is an optical one, so a fault on the load side cannot propagate into the controller, and the appliance needs no modification.

hyperedges.label: Safe Mains Actuation Pattern (isolation, contact fail-safe, appliance loads)
